intervals.note: Terminal event with an unknown date, given as a window: the earliest bound (March 1985) is June 1982 plus the '2.8 years of operation' of the 1985 ICRC paper, i.e. the detector was still running then; the latest bound (July 2004) is the review (arXiv v1, 26 Jul 2004) saying NUSEX 'stopped data-taking'. summary.plain: A 150-ton detector of iron plates and gas tubes in a cave beside the Mont Blanc road tunnel, under about five thousand metres of water-equivalent rock. It began running in 1982 to look for protons decaying, recorded a few proton-decay candidate events, none confirmed, and measured the atmospheric-neutrino flux.
summary.technical: Digital tracking calorimeter: 136 iron plates (1 cm) interleaved with resistive-cathode plastic streamer tubes read out by orthogonal strips, 150 t total, at about 5000 m.w.e. in the Mont Blanc tunnel; data from 1 June 1982. By 1985: 31 fully contained events in 2.8 years, 3 nucleon-decay candidates, the rest attributed to neutrino interactions; later atmospheric-neutrino analysis found the mu-neutrino flux in agreement with predictions.
